Same shell, IEC inlet instead of the terminal block.","kind":"orderable","part-numbers":{"AS7946-74XKSB-O-AC-F":{"part":"FNPEC7946008Z"}}},"dc-psu":{"default":true,"description":"Modular dual DC PSUs, front-to-back airflow. This is the unit we photographed.","kind":"orderable","part-numbers":{"AS7946-74XKSB-O-DC-F":{"part":"FNPEC7946007Z"}}}},"description":"Edgecore AGR420 (AS7946-74XKSB) 25GbE aggregation router. 2RU, 74 fixed ports - 2 x 100G QSFP-DD, 8 x 40/100G QSFP28 and 64 x 10/25G SFP28 - with a timing block, 1+1 redundant PSUs and 4+1 redundant fans.","format":1,"gaps":[{"blocks":[],"note":"The QSG's Front LEDs section tables every port family and every system lamp with a colour, and for the management jack says only \"RJ-45 OOB Port - Left (link), Right (activity)\". No colour, and no behaviour. The AGR420 datasheet has no LED section at all, so the QSG is the only source we hold. The two lamps therefore declare what the guide does say - the right lamp blinks for activity, which is the behaviour the same guide gives every other activity lamp on this device - and the left lamp keeps led-rect's generic off/on rather than an invented green-for-link. The AGR400's QSG (AS7946-30XB-QSG-R04) prints the identical sentence, so this is Edgecore's house style for the OOB jack and not a gap in one revision.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["mgmt-leds"],"wanted":"a NOS LED table, or photographs of the OOB jack with a link up and traffic running","what":"mgmt-led-colours"},{"blocks":[],"note":"The datasheet states \"Power Consumption - Max: 692 W, Typical: 201 W\" with no ambient. The QSG for the same SKU states \"527 W at 25 C, 723 W at 45 C\". Most of that is explained by ambient rather than by disagreement - 527 W at 25 C sits comfortably below the datasheet maximum - but the 45 C figure EXCEEDS the stated maximum by 31 W, and 45 C is the top of this device's own rated operating range (0 to 45 C), so the figure at that ambient should BE the maximum. 692 W is kept as the datasheet's own maximum.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["power-max-w"],"wanted":"an Edgecore statement of what ambient the datasheet's 692 W assumes, or a measurement at 45 C. Note that the QSG's 25 C figure here, 527 W, is identical to the AGR400 datasheet's stated maximum, which may mean one of the four Edgecore figures is a copy error","what":"power-consumption-sources"},{"blocks":[],"note":"Searched and absent, which is why this is asserted rather than left to L27 to imply. Both documents we hold - the datasheet and the QSG - rate the AGR PSUs by INPUT only (\"DC Input: -40 to -75V, 40 A, per PS\"; \"AC Input: 100-120 V 12 A or 200-240 V 7.5 A per PS\") and state no output wattage anywhere. The fan module gets no power figure at all. Unlike the Casa PEMs, these PSUs genuinely CONVERT, so `power-output-w` is the right key for them and the only thing missing is the number - which is exactly why it must not be derived from the input current, where 12 A at 100-120 V and 7.5 A at 200-240 V give different products and neither is an output rating.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["edgecore/agr-psu-ac@1","edgecore/agr-psu-dc@1","edgecore/agr-fan@1"],"wanted":"a photograph of either PSU's nameplate, which is where this figure normally lives, or an Edgecore part datasheet for the PSU and fan FRUs rather than for the chassis. The 550 W CRPS nameplate already in working/intake is the worked example of what would close it","what":"fru-power-unpublished"}],"groups":{"bracket-holes":{"index-origin":0,"role":"furniture","term":"Hole"},"fans":{"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"fasteners":{"index-origin":0,"role":"furniture","term":"Rivet"},"filters":{"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Filter"},"grounding":{"index-origin":0,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"labels":{"index-origin":0,"role":"furniture","term":"Label"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":0,"mixed":"the management corner - out-of-band RJ45, RS-232 console on micro-USB-B, a USB-A service port and the recessed reset. One cluster on the faceplate, four media","role":"management","term":"Port"},"mgmt-leds":{"description":"QSG Front LEDs callout 5 - \"RJ-45 OOB Port - Left (link), Right (activity)\". That is the whole of what the guide says. It gives these two lamps NO colour, so none is declared for them and the block has no shared vocabulary to declare either","index-origin":0,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfp-link-leds":{"description":"QSG Front LEDs callouts 1 and 2 - LED2 - Blue (all lanes linked / link), Off (not all lanes linked), Blinking (activity). Two things to note. Off is a MEANING on this lamp, not the absence of one: a partly linked QSFP reads dark, where the AGR400 lights the same condition Red, so the two sisters differ and `off` carries the sentence here. And the guide words the lit state differently for the two families - \"all lanes linked\" for QSFP-DD, \"link\" for QSFP28 - while the Traditional Chinese text of the same guide says \"all lanes linked\" for both; one vocabulary is modelled, named `linked`","index-origin":0,"role":"indicator","states":["off",{"color":"#3b82f6","name":"linked"},{"behavior":"blinking","name":"activity"}],"term":"LED"},"qsfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp28","speed":"100g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"qsfp28-speed-leds":{"description":"QSG Front LEDs callout 2 - LED1 (left of each pair) - Blue (100G), Green (40G)","index-origin":0,"role":"indicator","states":["off",{"color":"#3b82f6","name":"100g"},{"color":"#22c55e","name":"40g"}],"term":"LED"},"qsfpdd-100g":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp-dd","speed":"100g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"qsfpdd-speed-leds":{"description":"QSG Front LEDs callout 1 - LED1 (top) - Blue (100G). The QSFP-DD ports run at one rate here, so this lamp has one lit state and the guide names no other","index-origin":0,"role":"indicator","states":["off",{"color":"#3b82f6","name":"100g"}],"term":"LED"},"sfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp28","speed":"25g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"sfp28-link-leds":{"description":"QSG Front LEDs callout 3 - LED2 (right of each pair) - Blue (link), Blinking (activity). The SFP28 lamp is NOT given the QSFP's \"Off (not all lanes linked)\" reading - a single-lane port has no partial link - so its off state means only unlit","index-origin":0,"role":"indicator","states":["off",{"color":"#3b82f6","name":"linked"},{"behavior":"blinking","name":"activity"}],"term":"LED"},"sfp28-speed-leds":{"description":"QSG Front LEDs callout 3 - LED1 (left of each pair) - Blue (25G), Green (10G)","index-origin":0,"role":"indicator","states":["off",{"color":"#3b82f6","name":"25g"},{"color":"#22c55e","name":"10g"}],"term":"LED"},"status-leds":{"description":"QSG Front LEDs callout 4 - Green (OK), Amber (fault). DIAG, FAN, PS0 and PS1 all read this way; LOC does not, and overrides it on its own placement","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","states":["off",{"color":"#22c55e","name":"ok"},{"color":"#f59e0b","name":"fault"}],"term":"LED"},"timing":{"index-origin":0,"mixed":"the timing block - BITS and 1PPS/ToD on RJ45 beside 10MHz and 1PPS on coax SMB. What makes it one block is the clock, not the connector, and the faceplate legends it as one","role":"management","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"Edgecore","maturity":"modelled","model":"AS7946-74XKSB","name":"as7946-74xksb","portfolio":{"family":"Aggregation Router","line":"Service Provider","series":"AGR420"},"provenance":{"airflow":"datasheet - both listed SKUs are front-to-back","audit-by-eye":"gate 5 - the front and rear were rendered at the reference figure's own px/mm (3947 and 3943 px wide) and compared strip by strip against it. Every cage row, every block gap, every pair legend and every LED strip lands on the reference; the numbering was confirmed as far out as the 36/37 legend rather than being trusted from block A alone. Two things were moved because of this pass and not before it: the rear PSU pair and grounding plate, and the top filter's left thumb screw","audit-by-name":"gate 5 - all thirteen datasheet page-2 callouts walked and satisfied. 1 -> port-0/1; 2 -> port-2..9; 3 -> port-10..73; 4 -> bits-0/1/2; 5 -> mhz-10-in; 6 -> usb; 7 -> mgmt-eth with led-mgmt-link and led-mgmt-act; 8 -> console-1; 9 -> pps-tod; 10 -> pps-1-out; 11 -> console-0; 12 -> psu-0/psu-1 bays with dc-psu and ac-psu configurations; 13 -> fan-0..fan-4. From the QSG on top of those: the grounding point -> ground-plate, the reset button -> reset, the five system LEDs -> led-diag/loc/fan/ps0/ps1, and the Air Filter Replacement procedure -> filter-top, filter-top-step, filter-bottom-step and filter-bottom. From the photographs: four corner captive screws -> panel-screw-0..3, and the top-cover labels -> label-spec, label-serial, label-caution. 324 placements and bays in all, 74 ports and 148 port lamps among them. Nothing in either document is unaccounted for","chassis":"datasheet - \"Dimensions (WxDxH): 440 mm x 480 mm x 87 mm (2RU)\". The QSG Chassis section gives the same 440 x 480 x 87 mm (17.3 x 18.9 x 3.4 in), so unlike the AGR400 the two Edgecore documents agree and no disagreement has to be carried","color":"photo - the same dark grey painted steel as the AGR400, which is the same shell","depth":"measured - 480 mm, and the AGR400 model's 524 mm is believed WRONG. The AGR400 and the AGR420 are the SAME SHELL, not two shells: the bottom pans in IMG_6792 (AGR400) and IMG_6812 (AGR420) are the same stamping - the same dimple pattern, the same PSU and fan cut-out at one corner, the same rivet lines - and the top, side and rear metalwork matches as well. One shell can only have one depth. Three of the four Edgecore documents say 480 (both AGR420 documents and the AGR400 datasheet); only the AGR400 quick start guide says 524, and that is the outlier. It is not an over-handles figure either: the rear PSU and fan handles project about 17 mm past the rear panel, photo-measured in IMG_6810, not the 44 mm the difference would need. This model uses 480 for every face. The AGR400 model still carries 524 and should be corrected to match","fan-labels":"photo - the datasheet figure prints FAN 4 to FAN 0 vertically beside each bay. The real device (IMG_6809) prints them horizontally BELOW each bay with an airflow arrow to their left, the same as the AGR400. The real device wins","fans":"drawing plus Jason - the fan bays keep the AGR400 geometry, 69.4 mm square on a 70.4 mm pitch. This figure reads 68.5 mm pitch, 2.7 percent smaller, which is inside figure error, and the AGR400 number has the stronger derivation - it is the only size that is both square, as the photographs show, and fits its measured pitch. Overlaid at matched scale the five bays land on the reference","filters":"drawing plus photo - the AGR420 front carries a top and a bottom air filter, and NEITHER is the AGR400 part. Checked before assuming, as asked: edgecore/agr-filter-top@1 is 353.5 mm wide against the 417 needed here, and it is stepped for the AGR400's TWO QSFP-DD blocks where this front has ONE, at the left. Three new components were drawn - agr420-filter-top (417.0 x 8.6 at panel 12.5, 1.0), agr420-filter-bottom (399.5 x 9.0 at 12.5, 77.5) and agr420-filter-step (25.5 x 16.5, placed twice, at 12.5, 10.7 and 12.5, 61.0). Each physical filter is ONE part with a stepped frame and appears as two placements: a placement is a bounding rectangle to both the renderer and lint rule L13, so a single 26 mm stepped box would read as sitting on top of the sixteen ports it steps around. Both halves carry group `filters` and their descriptions say which whole they belong to","grounding":"photo - an IEC earth symbol with a two-hole plate beneath it, immediately right of the PSU bays, visible in IMG_6809. edgecore/agr-ground-plate@1 draws exactly this","indicators":"the five system LEDs and the RST button carry no `for:` and lint warns (L19). That is correct here and matches the AGR400: DIAG and LOC are chassis-wide, and PS0/PS1 annotate psu-0 and psu-1, which are bays in the REAR view - L14 requires a `for:` target in the SAME view, so naming them would trade a warning for an error","labels":"photo - RECTANGULAR. common/device-label is an oval recess belonging to another platform and is deliberately not used. The artwork is placeholder blocks: the real serial, SKU and MAC addresses are legible in IMG_6808 and are NOT transcribed","led-states":"QSG Front LEDs section, callouts 1 to 5, re-read off the guide rather than trusted from the transcription. Every lens carries its function in attrs and its state vocabulary in structured states:, declared on the GROUP where a block shares one - two QSFP-DD speed lamps, eight QSFP28 speed lamps, sixty-four SFP28 speed lamps, ten QSFP link lamps and sixty-four SFP28 link lamps - and on the placement where it does not, which here is LOC and the management activity lamp. The sentence the guide prints sits beside them in description:. This was previously prose in attrs: {states: ...} on all 148 lamps, which no tool could read: the Explorer refuses a data-states value that is not a list of tokens, so what reached the chips was led-dot's generic off/on and the real 25G/10G vocabulary reached nobody. Three corrections from the re-read. LOC \"flashes Amber when the command is activated\" - the word \"locate\" was the modeller's gloss, the same slip the AGR400 had, and \"flashes\" is a behaviour the prose had dropped. The management lamps are given NO colour by the guide - \"Left (link), Right (activity)\" is all it says - where the attrs claimed \"Lit = link\"; nothing is declared for the link lamp rather than inventing one. And the QSFP link lamp's Off is a MEANING here, \"not all lanes linked\", where the AGR400 lights that same condition Red - the two sisters genuinely differ","mgmt-block":"drawing - a ganged 2x2 RJ-45 block at 356.0/372.3 by 14.4/28.2 carrying BITS 0 and BITS 2 above and BITS 1 and PPS/TOD below; two SMB jacks at x 393.6 and 394.1; USB Type A on its side centred at 407.2, 33.6; MGMT and CONSOLE 1 RJ-45s at 413.5; a micro-USB CONSOLE 0 at 402.9, 44.4 and a recessed RST button at 394.8, 44.6. The block is within 2 mm of the AGR400's in every position, which is what a shared shell predicts","other-faces":"photo - all four remaining faces were photographed and are modelled from those shots, not left blank. Top (IMG_6808): two rectangular labels near the front right and a caution notice at the rear left. Bottom (IMG_6812): rivets and formed dimples in five columns, no labels. Sides (IMG_6810 left, IMG_6811 right): a cluster of eight rack-bracket holes near the front and rivets along the length. Positions are photo-measured against the 440 mm width and the 480 mm depth and are approximate - none of these shots is orthographic","panel-screws":"drawing - four captive slotted thumb screws about 8.4 mm across at the panel corners, Hough-detected at (5.8, 13.5), (5.8, 73.6) and (433.9, 5.8); the fourth, at (433.9, 81.2), is hidden behind a callout arrow in the figure and is taken from IMG_6807 and from the symmetry of the other three. common/screw-head is 3.6 mm and reads as a machine screw at this size, so edgecore/agr-panel-screw was drawn for them","part-numbers":"datasheet Ordering Information - AS7946-74XKSB-O-DC-F is FNPEC7946007Z and AS7946-74XKSB-O-AC-F is FNPEC7946008Z","port-0-1-legend":"drawing + photo - the 0 up down 1 legend is NOT in the top band with the others. The QSFP-DD column stands alone at the left, and the datasheet page-2 front figure and IMG_6807 both show its legend printed on the metal step between the air filter and the top aperture, not above the filter. Placed at baseline 30.20, which is the same 1.10mm above the aperture that every other column on this panel uses; the step edge measures 27.1 in the photograph against the 27.2 this model already had, so the band it sits in is 4.1mm tall and the glyphs clear both edges. It was at 13.50, under filter-top-step, where nothing could read it","port-count":"datasheet - callouts 1 to 3 on the page-2 figure: 2 x 100G QSFP-DD, 8 x 100G QSFP28, 64 x 25GE SFP28. 2 + 8 + 64 = 74, matching the model number","port-cutouts":"drawing - one cutout per aperture, 74 of them, sized from the module footprint rather than the registry aperture because ganged cages abut: 18.5 x 9.58 for QSFP and 14.25 x 10.4 for SFP28. The registry apertures (19.0 x 10.0 and 14.5 x 10.0) are single-port figures and would overlap at the measured 14.25 mm pitch","port-leds":"drawing plus datasheet - the QSG Front LEDs section gives two LEDs per port on all three families, and the ARRANGEMENT DIFFERS BY FAMILY. QSFP-DD: LED1 top, LED2 bottom, a stacked pair OUTSIDE the block at x 12.6, at y 36.6/39.7 for port 0 and 45.6/48.7 for port 1. QSFP28 and SFP28: LED1 left, LED2 right, as arrow-shaped light pipes in the white strip BETWEEN the two rows of a pair - centres at column x + 1.35, 3.75, 13.55, 15.95 for QSFP28 and + 1.95, 4.85, 8.85, 11.75 for SFP28, on strips centred at panel y 28.4 and 57.8. Within each pair of marks the DOWN arrow serves the port below the strip and the UP arrow the port above it, so a strip carries four lamps for two ports. The strip is 6.4 mm tall and the marks were read at 7x before being assigned. The QSFP28 offsets are nudged 0.15 mm apart from the 1.50/3.45/13.70/15.70 that were read off the render, because common/led-arrow-sm is 2.25 mm wide and two lamps 1.95 mm apart overlap; 0.15 is well inside the +/- 0.3 mm this figure can be read to","port-numbering":"drawing - the pair legends read \"N up down M\" with the up arrow belonging to the LEFT number and the down arrow to the right, the same convention as the AGR400, read at 7x on the 600 dpi render. Numbering runs down each column four at a time: ports 0-1 are the QSFP-DD, 2-5 the left QSFP28 column and 6-9 the right, then the SFP28 run 10-73 block by block and column by column. The last legend, 72 up down 73, is legible on the real device in IMG_6807 at the bottom right, which confirms the scheme end to end","ports":"drawing - four cage rows whose tops sit at panel y 14.6, 31.3, 44.3 and 61.0. The QSFP-DD pair occupies the middle two rows in a single column at x 16.1; the eight QSFP28 sit in two abutting columns at x 44.6 and 63.1, four rows deep; the 64 SFP28 sit in four blocks of four columns, the blocks starting at x 90.35, 156.32, 222.29 and 288.26 on a 65.97 mm pitch and the columns inside each block on a 14.25 mm pitch, which is exactly the std/sfp-ganged footprint - ganged cages abut","psu-width":"CARRIED FORWARD, not resolved - edgecore/agr-psu-dc@1 and agr-psu-ac@1 are 60.1 mm wide, and the callout box drawn round the PSU pair measures 57.9 mm on the AGR400 datasheet page and 53.6 mm here. The component may be a little over. It is reused unchanged because Jason confirmed both platforms take the same PSU and narrowing it would silently move the AGR400; the disagreement is recorded rather than acted on","rear":"drawing plus Jason - two stacked PSU bays at the left, a grounding landing, then five fan bays. The PSU pair is placed from THIS device's figure, not the AGR400's: both Edgecore datasheet rear figures put the PSU block's left edge at panel x 13-14 (12.82 on the AGR400 page, 14.06 here), while the AGR400 model has it at 6.26 measured off that router's QSG, and at 6.26 the PSU0/PSU1 legend would be printed under the bay. The bays here start at 11.5 and the grounding plate moves right to 71.8, which is where IMG_6809 and the figure both put it. The AGR400 rear should be re-checked","rj45-choice":"Jason - use std/ before common/. std/rj45 is the IEC 60603-7 aperture; the hand-drawn common/rj45-shielded puts its integrated LEDs on the contacts side, which no real jack does. All six jacks are std/rj45@1, and MGMT's two LEDs are placed on top of it","rj45-orientation":"drawing - BITS 0, BITS 2, MGMT and CONSOLE 1 are keyway-UP; only BITS 1 and PPS/TOD, the lower row of the ganged block, are keyway-down. A 2-high ganged jack mirrors its rows so both release tabs stay reachable. std/rj45 draws keyway-down, so the other four carry rotate 180","ru":"datasheet - 87 mm is 2 RU","scale":"drawing - the datasheet page-2 Interfaces figures are orthographic. The front panel measures 3947 x 775 px on a 600 dpi render, an aspect of 5.093 against the datasheet 440/87 = 5.057, a 0.7 percent match; the rear measures 3943 x 772, an aspect of 5.108. Both carry geometry, and everything below is measured off them at 8.9705 px/mm across and 8.9080 px/mm down","sources":"datasheet AGR420-AS7946-74XKSB-DS-R03 and quick start guide AS7946-74XKSB-QSG-R03, both Edgecore, plus six photographs of a real unit (IMG_6807 front, 6808 top, 6809 rear, 6810 left, 6811 right, 6812 bottom) and Edgecore's stock renders. No mechanical drawing was available","spec-table":"datasheet - silicon, external TCAM, CPU, memory, flash, SSD, BMC, capacity, timing, power and environmentals transcribed into attrs. Where the datasheet and the QSG disagree - weight 16 vs 15.3 kg, max power 692 vs 527/723 W - both numbers are carried rather than one being silently chosen","status-leds":"drawing - DIAG, LOC, FAN, PS0 and PS1 on a 4.75 mm pitch beneath the timing block at y 45.0, legends beneath them at 48.9","top-view-orientation":"the top and bottom views put y = 0 at the REAR, following the AGR400, whose caution label sits at y 26 and is described there as being at the rear left.
